style_instructions: Favor sharper adult-adjacent, risky, absurd twists; push beyond mild puns and moderate escalations. Keep semantic legibility: the replacement must clearly make sense in the original title context and produce a coherent new premise. Avoid opaque misspellings or invented words whose meaning is not immediately clear. Choose changed words with strong phonetic similarity to the original but an immediate, bold meaning shift—sex, bodily fluids, violence, drugs, money, chaos, taboo, power dynamics, or other provocative stakes. Prefer concrete absurd premises over clever wordplay alone. If a title contains a common noun, mutate it into something more edgy and unexpected while preserving grammar and recognizability. For each movie, draft multiple wild variants, then select the one that is funniest because the premise itself escalates, not merely because of the pun. Reject candidates whose humor depends on spelling confusion or a weak connection.
